PullRequest.Title: Disable newly added flaky "concurrent hosts converge on one compute identity" test

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the Mission Control WPS Node test suite containing the parameterized concurrent compute-identity cases
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the diff, suite completion waited for all five initial-state cases, including each case's concurrent configure wave and restart configure. After test.skip, none of the test bodies execute, so this work is absent from the test critical path. Product startup and Mission Control runtime paths are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and remove a temporary directory, optionally seed identity records, perform identity-file reads/writes during 10 concurrent service configurations plus one restart configuration, then read the persisted record and directory entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five parameterized initial states; previously one temporary directory and 11 configure calls per state (55 configure calls total), with state-dependent setup writes. The exact internal filesystem-call count per configure depends on identity state and contention.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All five cases executed their filesystem setup, concurrent identity initialization, persisted-record validation, and cleanup. The diff suppresses those existing calls rather than adding or moving a boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously these operations had to finish for the test suite to complete; the changed skip removes them entirely from execution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed test matrix of five identity states and 10 concurrent hosts per state, yielding 50 concurrent-wave configurations plus five restart configurations; no user-controlled or production collection scales this change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Before the diff, each case issued 10 service.configure calls through Promise.all, followed by one serialized restart configure; test-runner scheduling between parameterized cases follows the existing suite runner. After the diff, effective concurrency for these cases is zero.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cases covered cold/migration states (missing, legacy, copied, interrupted, completed) and a warm restart reading the persisted identity. Skipping them removes both cold and warm test execution; it does not alter production cache keys, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sole changed line replaces test with test.skip, and the complete body uses test fakes for fetch/socket behavior while real filesystem work is now not invoked.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact CI time and internal filesystem operation count are not measured, but the direction is unambiguous: the diff removes work. There is no uncertainty about product-path reachability because only a test registration changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff reduces CI test work and does not change production behavior; reduced concurrency coverage is a correctness/testing concern outside the performance-review scope.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file, one-hunk diff and traced the skipped parameterized test's filesystem and concurrency behavior. The only performance effect is removal of test-only work; no runtime latency, CPU, memory, I/O, network, IPC, subprocess, rendering, or cache regression is introduced.
